subject: USAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB495 landed the ONE derivation of an elementary item's EFFECTIVE usage -- its own USAGE clause, else the nearest enclosing group's (13.18.60.4 GR1) -- feeding the group-header shed, the leaf's representation and EVERY 13.18.60.3 screen through the SAME code the written-clause path runs (PictureAnalyzer.ScreenUsageAgainstPicture, extracted for the purpose). The invariant is stated and locked as an EQUIVALENCE rather than as cases: `01 G USAGE u. 05 A <pic>.` and `01 G. 05 A <pic> USAGE u.` are the same item, so they must produce the same verdict, the same diagnostic code and the same width, for EVERY member of the Usage enum. UsageInheritanceDriftTests enumerates the enum and asserts exactly that (24 members x 6 pictures x 2 arms). MEASURED on the pre-fix tree 39479e19: 108 of those 138 cells DIFFERED between the two arms; after the fix, 0 differ. BOTH LIMBS NOW HOLD, and the two holes the row recorded are closed together because the extraction made them one site. LIMB 2 ("an elementary data item SUBORDINATE TO A GROUP ITEM whose declaration contains" the usage) had no site: `01 G USAGE COMP. 05 A PIC X(3).` compiled and A stayed a 3-byte alphanumeric DISPLAY item with the COMP silently dropped. It now reports the SAME COBOL0881 as the written-clause spelling, from the same code. THE NUMERIC-EDITED HOLE (kb/Work PB540) is closed in the same change: the screen's predicate was `anyAlpha`, so `PIC ZZ9 USAGE COMP` escaped it and bound as a 1-byte binary item against a 3-character image; writing the rule properly in the extracted screen -- SR3 admits only "a picture character-string that describes a NUMERIC item", and 8.5.2 Table 2 puts category numeric alone in class numeric while numeric-EDITED is class alphanumeric -- rejects it on both arms and recovers to usage-display, so the item measures 3 like the usage-less control. Measured at 85/2002/2014/2023.
